chunks: Do you not see that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures and many of the people? And many upon whom the punishment is due. And whoever Allah humiliates - for him is there no bestower of honor. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the verse says the sun, moon, and mountains prostrate to God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Hajj is often interpreted through the lens of 'sujud al-takwini' (ontological submission), where all entities, including the sun and moon, naturally bow to Allah's command, contrasting with 'sujud al-taklifi' (voluntary submission) required of humans. The mention of 'many people' facing punishment highlights the distinction between those who recognize this universal order and those who defy it, underscoring Allah's absolute sovereignty (Al-Muqtadir). This duality serves as a reminder that while creation is compelled to submit, human beings possess the free will to choose between gratitude and ingratitude.
